Subject: MSA redlines — liability cap & trade secrets

Hi Lauren / Rishi,

Thanks for sending the MSA. Our legal team at NovaHealth has a hard requirement: carve out willful misappropriation of trade secrets from the general liability cap and a separate allocation for reasonable forensics and mitigation costs. They want language that ensures (1) the cap does not apply where there is a court-ordered finding or contractual admission of misappropriation, and (2) Redwood reimburses for externally incurred forensics and preservation costs incurred to investigate an exfiltration event.

Two practical asks from our side: can you confirm Redwood can (a) produce forensics-support artifacts within 72 hours of a preservation notice and (b) preserve relevant logs and snapshots for at least 90 days? NovaLegal will also want a narrow definition of "trade secret" and an evidentiary standard (e.g., court finding or comparable proof) so this isn't an open-ended escape hatch.

I've attached our redline (NovaHealth_MSA_redlines_v2.pdf) and Greg (outside counsel) is on copy. Please let us know your suggested language or any counter-proposals by COB Wednesday — we have a procurement / security gating review Thursday morning.

Best,
Ellen Park
Director, Vendor Risk & Compliance
NovaHealth

Ellen — thanks for the clear note and the redlines.

High level response / proposal from Redwood: we are open to a tightly scoped exception to the liability cap for proven trade secret misappropriation, but only where the following are true:
- There is either (i) a final judgment, (ii) an interlocutory injunction specifically finding misappropriation, or (iii) a written admission by the customer;
- The claim arises from willful and knowing exfiltration of trade secret data (not negligence or access incidents without misappropriation); and
- Redwood's liability for such claims will be limited to direct damages arising from the misappropriation plus documented, reasonable forensics and mitigation costs (we would exclude punitive / consequential damages to the extent permitted by law).

Operational point: Redwood can commit to making preserved artifacts available within 72 hours where a preservation notice is validly served and we can preserve logs/snapshots for 90 days when customers opt into the enhanced retention add-on. (Default retention is shorter; we can add an optional retention rider to the order form.)

I'll have Rishi draft focused contract language and Karthik provide a brief forensics runbook / evidence checklist to attach as an exhibit. Proposed next step: I will circulate a short excerpt for your review today so procurement has something to gate on tomorrow.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 21, 2027 at 9:03 AM lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai> wrote:
> I'll have Rishi draft focused contract language and Karthik provide a brief forensics runbook / evidence checklist to attach as an exhibit.

Quick technical notes for Ellen / NovaHealth — these will inform the exhibit:
- What we can produce: audit logs (auth, model invocation metadata, tenant IDs), persisted object snapshots (if customer uses persistent storage), model KV cache metadata (limited; not full private memory), and network flow logs for the time period requested.
- What we cannot reasonably produce: ephemeral GPU memory dumps post-eviction, decrypted in-memory model weights, or end-user plaintext from transient caches unless instrumented retention was configured ahead of time.
- Timing: 72 hours to triage and provide initial artifacts is feasible for standard logs; full forensic reproducibility (snapshots, cross-region retrievals) may take longer depending on data tiering and whether the customer has retention add-on enabled.
- Retention recommendation: 90 days for logs related to security events, with a 30-day hold extension on a preservation notice.

I'll attach the Forensics-Process-SLA.xlsx which outlines timelines and sample artifact types we can commit to. We should include language allowing Redwood to charge for extraordinary preservation requests if they require retrieval from cold storage.

—Karthik

Ellen / Greg — attaching a draft excerpt that narrows the carve-out and sets an evidentiary gate. Key points in our draft:
- Definition: "Trade Secret" follows the Uniform Trade Secrets Act (or applicable state equivalent) and requires demonstrable secrecy measures by the customer;
- Gate: Cap exception only triggers upon (a) final adjudication, (b) a court order granting injunctive relief based on misappropriation, or (c) a written admission of misappropriation;
- Remedies: Redwood will be responsible for direct damages arising from the misappropriation and for reasonable, documented forensic and mitigation costs (capped at the lesser of actual costs or $250k per event unless otherwise agreed);
- Cooperation: Customer must provide timely preservation notice and reasonable access to assist investigations; Redwood may invoice for exceptional retrieval from cold storage.

Next steps: please review MSA_v1.3_redline_for_signoff.pdf and let me know any material objections. If we get alignment today I can finalize language and circulate a clean order-form addendum for signatures.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
